audit.whatIsWrong: All seven full-layer phases[].side read "Skill" while content win[] and packet.levelChart both read Ekko on rows 0-5 and Anivia on 2+ items.
audit.why: Two sources agree against the full layer, and the kits back it: Anivia has no dash anywhere, so Ekko's E dictates every early trade; Rebirth plus Glacial Storm is what flips it late.
audit.corrected: phases[0..5]=Ekko, phases[6]=Anivia, each why rewritten to argue the same verdict; ratings moved to 6/10 early and 4/10 on the late row.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes was the generic template and put the turn at level 6; the real turn in this lane is late, on Rebirth and Glacial Storm.
audit.why: Level 6 gives Anivia zoning but no mobility, so it changes nothing about who can leave a fight. The late row is the only one that moves.
audit.corrected: Spikes rewritten to immobility 1-5 / 6 changes nothing for her / late Rebirth returns a health bar.

audit.whatIsWrong: content mid told the reader they "can still engage through or around her Crystallize wall with your dash on E". Crystallize is 'an impassable wall of ice to block all movement' — the E dash does not cross it. Separately, the single most useful rule in this matchup was never stated: Frostbite deals DOUBLE damage only to a target recently hit by Flash Frost or damaged by a fully formed Glacial Storm.
audit.why: Both are verbatim from Riot's text. The first is advice that gets the reader killed; the second is what makes sidestepping the sphere worth doing.
audit.corrected: content mid rewritten to bait the 17s wall instead of dashing it; the Frostbite doubling condition written into enemyWin, tradeGood, report[5], dosFull[0], dontsFull[0] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rebirth was mentioned only as a late-game scaling note. It changes every all-in in the lane: killing Anivia means killing two full health bars.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Upon taking fatal damage, Anivia reverts to an egg and is reborn with full health.'
audit.corrected: Written into ahead, breakdown.carry, breakdown.late, dontsFull[2].d and phases[6].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit in it (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT) and ended on two near-identical filler clauses about R.
audit.why: It is the field that carries the real numbers.
audit.corrected: Flash Frost 11s down to 7s, Crystallize a flat 17s, Frostbite a flat 4s, Chronobreak 110s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: 17 lint findings: 12 misgenderings of Anivia, 2 copy-paste bleeds (dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[2].d), 1 numberless cooldowns field.

notes:
CHART: all seven full-layer phases[].side read 'Skill' while content win[] and packet.levelChart agreed on Ekko x6 then Anivia at 2+ items. I moved the full layer onto the content layer, so no win[N] edits were possible (before would equal after). Every side edit carries a rewritten why; ratings moved with the verdicts.

DANGEROUS ADVICE REMOVED: content mid said you can 'engage through or around her Crystallize wall with your dash on E'. Riot's W text is 'an impassable wall of ice to block all movement' — the dash does not cross it. Replaced with baiting the flat 17s and entering while it melts.

ADDED, the rule this lane actually runs on: Frostbite doubles ONLY against a target recently hit by Flash Frost or damaged by a fully formed Glacial Storm. Nothing on the page said what the sidestep was buying. Also added Rebirth as an all-in cost — killing Anivia is two full health bars, which changes when you spend Chronobreak.

SUSPECT NAME: packet flags wants.foe[1] 'Use Crystallize' — false positive, that is her real W name. No edit.

REPORT SWEEP: one substantive rewrite (report[5]). report[0]/[3]/[4]/[11] are lint-mandated pronoun corrections carried in step with their source fields.

LEFT ALONE (templated, nothing Anivia-specific to ground them without inventing): report[10], report[12], report[9], content early and late (both already accurate), wants.*.

UNVERIFIED, not written: Rebirth's cooldown and egg duration are not in the kit file, so I wrote 'a second full health bar' and never a timer; whether Ekko's Chronobreak arrival damage can break the egg; and whether Crystallize blocks the Chronobreak return path. Left out of every field.
